subject: Private deployment feasibility + hyperscaler comparison — next tests & MAP
messages:
From: Alan Pierce <alan.pierce@govdata-sys.gov>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 15:03:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up from today's call — private deploy feasibility + hyperscaler comparisons

Thanks for the demo this morning, Stephanie. Helpful session — I wanted to capture three specific items our security and infra teams flagged and ask for concrete next steps:

1) Control plane networking: we need a clear statement of what outbound connections Redwood Private requires (IPs/domains/ports) and whether there's an option to proxy those through our egress-only gateways. We run strict allow-lists.

2) Air-gapped mode feasibility: we heard there are two private modes. Can you confirm whether fully air-gapped (no outbound control plane) deployments are supported today for inference workloads, and if so what limitations (updates, telemetry, model onboarding) apply?

3) HSM/KMS and audit logs: we need to know supported KMS integrations (PKCS#11? cloud KMS?), key rotation processes, and what audit logs Redwood will expose for a private install.

If you can send a concise checklist for each item and suggest the minimal tests we should run to validate, that would help us scope the POC. Attaching our security_requirements_v2.pdf for reference.

—Alan
Deputy CTO, GovData Systems
security@govdata-sys.gov

[Attachment: security_requirements_v2.pdf (pdf, 88KB)]

From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>

Cc: dev_patel@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Follow-up from today's call — private deploy feasibility + hyperscaler comparisons

Alan — thanks for the clear list and for sharing the security doc. Short answer up-front: yes, we can support both an outbound-only control plane (recommended for most VPC customers) and an on-prem/local-control-plane air-gap mode, but they have different trade-offs. Below is a concise checklist and the minimal verification steps we recommend for your infra and security teams.

High-level checklist (quick read):
- Control plane connectivity: outbound-only by default. Required egress: TLS to a narrow set of FQDNs and ports (443) + optional cert pinning.
- Air-gapped mode: supported for inference-only workloads; requires local package repo for updates and an offline model onboarding workflow. Telemetry is opt-in and can be redirected to local SIEM.
- KMS/HSM: supports cloud KMS (GCP/AWS/Azure) and on-prem HSM via PKCS#11; bring-your-own keys supported.
- Audit logs: full request/response metadata, auth events, and admin actions — exported to S3-compatible storage or pushed to syslog/Elasticsearch.

Minimal validation tests we propose (we can run jointly or hand over to your infra team):
A) Network egress verification — we provide a small test container that attempts the exact outbound connections; you run it in your env and return the results.
B) Control plane proxy test — validate passing control plane traffic through your egress/proxy and confirm no ports beyond 443 are required.
C) Air-gap dry run — we do a staged test: onboard a small model artifact via an offline bundle you host, validate inference, and check that telemetry remains local.
D) KMS/HSM key unwrap test — integrate an HSM simulator (we provide config examples) and verify model keys can be used for encryption at rest and for in-flight signing.

Proposed timeline (2 weeks to run and observe):
- Week 1: Network egress verification + control plane proxy test
- Week 2: Air-gap dry run + KMS/HSM key integration test

Next steps for us: I'll coordinate with Dev and Vivek on the test artifacts and configs. Dev: can you add the IP/FQDN list + sample NAT/proxy config to the test bundle? Vivek: please draft the air-gap onboarding guide (offline bundle format + checksums).

Alan — if that timeline looks OK I can schedule the kickoff with your infra lead for Monday. Also attaching a short architecture diagram and a compact SOC2 excerpt that often helps procurement teams.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192

[Attachments: redwood-private-arch-diagram.pdf (pdf, 220KB), SOC2-compact.pdf (pdf, 75KB)]

Subject: Re: Follow-up from today's call — private deploy feasibility + hyperscaler comparisons

Stephanie — adding the technical details we should include in the test bundle. I kept this focused so GovData infra can lift-and-run:

1) Egress/Allow-list details:
- FQDNs: control.redwood.ai, metadata.redwood.ai, pkg.redwood.ai (we'll provide per-POC FQDN/IP overrides)
- Ports: 443 outbound only (no other persistent ports required).
- TLS: mTLS option available for control plane (mutual certs).
- If GovData requires an egress proxy, the traffic is standard HTTPS; we support CONNECT tunnels and can provide explicit proxy auth examples.

2) Air-gap/local control plane notes:
- Mode: local-control-plane (no outbound by default). Requires an initial offline bundle (tarball) that contains: runtime RPMs/containers, model artifacts, policy file, and checksums.
- Updates: offline package repo mechanism. Security team must approve bundle; patches are applied by re-running the bundle installer.
- Telemetry: disabled by default; if enabled it writes locally to configured syslog/ELK endpoint.
- Limitations: no hosted autoupdate, no hosted model catalog; MLOPS automation features are limited unless a sync bridge is later enabled.

3) KMS/HSM integration:
- Supported: AWS KMS (via role-assumed endpoints), GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault and PKCS#11-compatible HSMs.
- Keys: customer-managed keys for disk encryption + model artifact encryption.
- Rotation: keys can be rotated; we provide CLI utilities to rewrap keys under a new key with minimal downtime.

4) Test artifacts I'll attach:
- network-egress-test.tar (small container + curl script)
- proxy-config-example.conf (sample for Squid/Bluecoat)
- hsm-sim-config.tgz (HSM simulator + PKCS#11 test harness)

I also added a short checklist for the air-gap dry-run in MVP-test-plan.xlsx (will attach). Vivek — can you review the offline bundle checklist and confirm the exact artifact names and checksum algorithm (we currently use sha256).

- Dev
Dev Patel
Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.ai

MAP (proposed)
- Kickoff (govdata infra + redwood eng): Monday 2026-11-15 — 60 min walkthrough of test scope and handoff.
- Deliverable #1 (by Fri 2026-11-13): network-egress-test.tar + proxy-config-example.conf + FQDN/IP allow-list.

- Deliverable #3 (by Mon 2026-11-16): HSM simulator config + PKCS#11 example for KMS integration test.
- Observation window: we recommend a 7-day observation after each test to capture telemetry & audit samples.

Acceptance criteria (simple):
- Network test: outbound connections from your environment to our test FQDNs succeed through your egress proxy (if present) and no other ports are opened.
- Air-gap test: offline bundle installs and inference runs for a sample 350M model; telemetry remains local when disabled.
- KMS test: HSM simulator completes a key unwrap and we confirm encryption at rest for artifacts.

Logistics/questions for you:
1) Who should we invite to the kickoff from GovData infra (name + email + timezone)?
2) Do you have an existing HSM vendor or should we use the simulator for the POC?

I'll attach the HubSpot playbook link for this opportunity and the Drive folder where we'll stage artifacts. If you confirm the kickoff time I'll send a calendar invite (we're showing availability Mon 11/15 09:00–11:00 PT).

Thanks — looking forward to running the tests.
